title: DR1 asks for a microchip number on horses, cats, dogs and ferrets; the frontend has no microchip field anywhere in the service.

finding.frontend: A person identifying an animal is offered at most four identifier types — passport, tattoo, ear tag and horse name — and which of them appear is decided by four commodity allowlists in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/services/commodities/stub.js:107-113. There is no microchip field on any commodity, and no microchip obligation exists to render one: the six unit-record identifier obligations in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js:113-198 are passport, tattoo, ear tag, horse name and the two free-text fallbacks.
finding.prototype: DR1 asks for a microchip on the two identifier sets a companion animal or an equine falls into. A horse (commodity code 0101) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Horse name, and a cat, dog, ferret or other live mammal (all commodity code 01061900) is asked for Microchip, Passport and Tattoo — app/data/commodity-identifiers.js:3-19. Microchip is the first field on both panels, so it is the identifier DR1 puts in front of the person first.
finding.difference: Add a microchip identifier to the per-animal record: a new unit-record obligation alongside the existing five in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/obligations/sections/commodities/identifiers.js, a MICROCHIP_COMMODITIES allowlist holding Horse, Cat and Dog in the stub's picker-name vocabulary, a label in the identification copy block, and the new obligation id added to the unit record's requires.anyOfIds so a microchip on its own satisfies the at-least-one-identifier rule. Adding it also widens the derived union behind specificIdentifierWhitelists, which is what stops a microchip-only commodity falling through to the free-text fallback fields.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a microchip field rendered on the frontend's horse, cat or dog identification panel, or finding that DR1's horse and 01061900 identifier sets do not include a Microchip entry.
finding.correction: The finding stands. The carried-over claim it rests on — that app/data/commodity-identifiers.js is release-agnostic, so a set written for DR2.1 also describes DR1 — was checked at the root mount and holds. The identification page resolves a species' fields through getIdentifierFieldsForSpecies (app/routes.js:1458-1471), which calls getIdentifiersForCommodityCode on the commodity's code and returns whatever that file holds; there is no release test anywhere on that path, no equivalent of the isDesignRelease21SessionData filter that getSearchCommodities applies to the commodity catalogue itself (app/routes.js:61-73), and the one release-conditional thing in the file — the germinal-product sets under 05119985 and 05111000 — is unreachable in DR1 because those commodities are never offered. Horse 0101 and companion-animal 01061900 are both in DR1's catalogue and both carry Microchip. Two things are read from source rather than seen: neither captured page holds a horse or a companion animal, so nobody has photographed a DR1 microchip field, and the claim that Microchip is 'the first field on both panels' is a reading of the template loop over the data order rather than an observation. Medium confidence is the right band, and the named control will not resolve to a crop on either captured screen.

relatedTo.why: the same per-commodity identifier sets; both are corrections to which identifier types a commodity is asked for
